claim: Drosophila R7 UV photoreceptors are divided into yellow (y) and pale (p) subtypes.
source: Drosophila R7 UV photoreceptors (PRs) are divided into yellow (y) and pale (p) subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the classification of R7 photoreceptors.

claim: yR7 PRs express the Dpr11 cell surface protein.
source: yR7 PRs express the Dpr11 cell surface protein and are presynaptic to Dm8 amacrine neurons (yDm8) that express Dpr11's binding partner DIP-γ
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-F.

claim: yR7 PRs are presynaptic to yDm8 amacrine neurons that express DIP-γ.
source: yR7 PRs express the Dpr11 cell surface protein and are presynaptic to Dm8 amacrine neurons (yDm8) that express Dpr11's binding partner DIP-γ
evidence: This connectivity pattern is described in the abstract and demonstrated through EM reconstruction and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: pR7 PRs synapse onto DIP-γ-negative pDm8.
source: while pR7 PRs synapse onto DIP-γ-negative pDm8
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by single-cell flipout experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: DIP-γ and dpr11 mutations affect the morphologies of yDm8 distal dendrites.
source: DIP-γ and dpr11 mutations affect the morphologies of yDm8 distal ('home column') dendrites.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones in Figure 5.

claim: yDm8 neurons are generated in excess during development and compete for presynaptic yR7 PRs.
source: yDm8 neurons are generated in excess during development and compete for presynaptic yR7 PRs
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by developmental time course experiments shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Interactions between Dpr11 and DIP-γ are required for yDm8 survival.
source: interactions between Dpr11 and DIP-γ are required for yDm8 survival
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through cell counting experiments in mutants shown in Figure 7.

claim: Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions allow yDm8 neurons to select yR7 PRs as their appropriate home column partners.
source: These interactions also allow yDm8 neurons to select yR7 PRs as their appropriate home column partners.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by gain-of-function experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 neurons do not normally compete for survival signals or R7 partners.
source: yDm8 and pDm8 neurons do not normally compete for survival signals or R7 partners
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by the fact that pDm8 numbers do not change when yDm8 are rescued with DIAP (Figure 7B).

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 neurons can be forced to compete by manipulation of R7 subtype fate.
source: but can be forced to do so by manipulation of R7 subtype fate
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experiments where R7 fates are altered (Figure 9).

claim: The Drosophila genome encodes about 1000 CSPs involved in cell-cell interactions.
source: The Drosophila genome encodes about 1000 CSPs involved in cell-cell interactions (Kurusu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a cited fact from the literature.

claim: Each neuronal type in the pupal visual system expresses more than 250 CSP genes.
source: A study of seven neuronal types in the pupal visual system found that each type expresses more than 250 of these CSP genes and differs from any of the other types by expression of least 50 genes (Tan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: The Dpr-ome has 21 2-IgSF domain Dpr proteins.
source: It has 21 2-IgSF domain Dpr proteins (Nakamura et al., 2002), each of which binds to one or more of the 11 3-IgSF DIP proteins.
evidence: This is a cited fact about the Dpr-ome composition.

claim: The Dpr-ome has 11 3-IgSF DIP proteins.
source: It has 21 2-IgSF domain Dpr proteins (Nakamura et al., 2002), each of which binds to one or more of the 11 3-IgSF DIP proteins.
evidence: This is a cited fact about the Dpr-ome composition.

claim: DIP and Dpr binding affinities vary between 1 and 200 µM.
source: Most DIPs interact with multiple Dprs and vice versa, and their binding affinities vary between 1 and 200 µM (Cheng et al., 2019a; Cosmanescu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from biochemical studies.

claim: In the pupal visual system, neurons expressing a DIP tend to be postsynaptic to neurons that express a Dpr to which that DIP binds in vitro.
source: In the pupal visual system, neurons expressing a DIP tend to be postsynaptic to neurons that express a Dpr to which that DIP binds in vitro (Carrillo et al., 2015; Cosmanescu et al., 2018; Davis et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited pattern observed in multiple studies.

claim: The five mammalian IgLON proteins are members of the Wirin family.
source: The five mammalian IgLON proteins are members of the Wirin family (Cheng et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is a cited classification from the literature.

claim: DIP-γ and Dpr11 regulate neuromuscular junction morphology in larvae.
source: DIP-γ and Dpr11 regulate neuromuscular junction (NMJ) morphology in larvae, and control survival of DIP-γ-expressing postsynaptic cells in the pupal optic lobe (OL) (Carrillo et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from previous studies.

claim: DIP-γ and Dpr11 control survival of DIP-γ-expressing postsynaptic cells in the pupal optic lobe.
source: DIP-γ and Dpr11 regulate neuromuscular junction (NMJ) morphology in larvae, and control survival of DIP-γ-expressing postsynaptic cells in the pupal optic lobe (OL) (Carrillo et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from previous studies.

claim: Interactions between postsynaptic DIP-α and presynaptic Dprs 6 and 10 control survival of postsynaptic OL neurons.
source: Interactions between postsynaptic DIP-α and presynaptic Dprs 6 and 10 also control survival of postsynaptic OL neurons, and can determine their synaptic connectivity patterns (Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study.

claim: DIP-α and Dpr10 control branching of DIP-α-expressing motor axons onto muscle fibers that express Dpr10.
source: In the larval and adult neuromuscular systems, however, DIP-α and Dpr10 control branching of DIP-α-expressing motor axons onto muscle fibers that express Dpr10 (Ashley et al., 2019; Cheng et al., 2019a; Venkatasubramanian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a cited finding from multiple studies.

claim: Dprs and DIPs regulate fasciculation and sorting of olfactory receptor neuron axons in the antennal lobe.
source: Dprs and DIPs regulate fasciculation and sorting of olfactory receptor neuron axons in the antennal lobe (Barish et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: In the lamina of the OL, DIPs prevent ectopic synapse formation.
source: In the lamina of the OL, DIPs prevent ectopic synapse formation (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: The Drosophila compound eye is composed of ~750 ommatidial units.
source: The Drosophila compound eye is composed of ~750 ommatidial units.
evidence: This is a stated fact about Drosophila eye anatomy.

claim: Each ommatidium contains eight photoreceptors that express different rhodopsins.
source: Each ommatidium contains eight photoreceptors (PRs) that express different rhodopsins (Rh).
evidence: This is a stated fact about ommatidial composition.

claim: Outer PRs (R1-R6) are used for motion detection.
source: Outer PRs (R1-R6) are used for motion detection, while the R7 and R8 inner PRs transmit chromatic information (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a stated functional distinction between PR types.

claim: R7 and R8 inner PRs transmit chromatic information.
source: Outer PRs (R1-R6) are used for motion detection, while the R7 and R8 inner PRs transmit chromatic information (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a stated functional distinction between PR types.

claim: R7 is a UV receptor.
source: R7 is a UV receptor, while R8 responds to visible light.
evidence: This is a stated functional property of R7.

claim: R8 responds to visible light.
source: R7 is a UV receptor, while R8 responds to visible light.
evidence: This is a stated functional property of R8.

claim: The optic lobe consists of the lamina, medulla and lobula complex.
source: Visual information received in the retina is transmitted to the OL, which consists of the lamina, medulla and lobula complex (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a stated anatomical fact about the optic lobe.

claim: The lamina and medulla are organized retinotopically.
source: The lamina and medulla are organized retinotopically, so that each point in visual space corresponds to one cartridge in the lamina and one column in the medulla.
evidence: This is a stated organizational principle of the visual system.

claim: p ommatidia (~35%) detect shorter wavelengths and have R7 that express Rh3 and R8 that express Rh5.
source: p ommatidia (~35%) detect shorter wavelengths, and have R7 that express the Rh3 (shorter-wave UV) rhodopsin and R8 that express Rh5 (blue)
evidence: This is a stated characteristic of pale ommatidia.

claim: y ommatidia (~65%) detect longer wavelengths and have R7 that express Rh4 and R8 that express Rh6.
source: while y ommatidia (~65%) detect longer wavelengths, and have R7 that express Rh4 (longer-wave UV) and R8 that express Rh6 (green).
evidence: This is a stated characteristic of yellow ommatidia.

claim: The R7 and R8 within an ommatidium mutually inhibit each other.
source: The R7 and R8 within an ommatidium mutually inhibit each other (Schnaitmann et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding about R7-R8 interactions.

claim: DRA ommatidia are found in two rows in the dorsal rim area of the eye and are important for polarized light detection.
source: A third type of ommatidia, 'DRA' is found in two rows in the dorsal rim area of the eye and is important for polarized light detection.
evidence: This is a stated fact about DRA ommatidia.

claim: Drosophila phototaxes to UV (R7) in preference to visible light (R8).
source: Drosophila phototaxes to UV (R7) in preference to visible light (R8).
evidence: This is a stated behavioral characteristic.

claim: Drosophila exhibits true color vision, being able to make intensity-independent discriminations among hues that differentially stimulate p and y R8 channels.
source: It also exhibits true color vision, being able to make intensity-independent discriminations among hues that differentially stimulate p and y R8 channels (Melnattur et al., 2014; reviewed by Song and Lee, 2018).
evidence: This is a cited behavioral capability.

claim: Dpr11 is selectively expressed by yR7 PRs.
source: In our earlier work, we showed that Dpr11 is selectively expressed by yR7 PRs, while its binding partner DIP-γ is expressed by a subset of Dm8 amacrine neurons (Carrillo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from previous work.

claim: DIP-γ is expressed by a subset of Dm8 amacrine neurons.
source: In our earlier work, we showed that Dpr11 is selectively expressed by yR7 PRs, while its binding partner DIP-γ is expressed by a subset of Dm8 amacrine neurons (Carrillo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from previous work.

claim: yR7 PRs specifically connect to DIP-γ-expressing Dm8 neurons (yDm8).
source: Here, we show that yR7 PRs specifically connect to DIP-γ-expressing Dm8 neurons (yDm8), while pR7 PRs connect to DIP-γ-negative Dm8 neurons (pDm8) in their respective y and p 'home columns'.
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments and EM reconstruction analysis.

claim: pR7 PRs connect to DIP-γ-negative Dm8 neurons (pDm8) in their respective home columns.
source: Here, we show that yR7 PRs specifically connect to DIP-γ-expressing Dm8 neurons (yDm8), while pR7 PRs connect to DIP-γ-negative Dm8 neurons (pDm8) in their respective y and p 'home columns'.
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments.

claim: There are separate 'yellow' and 'pale' circuits that could be used for discriminating long and short-wavelength UV inputs.
source: Analysis of the electron microscopic (EM) reconstruction of the medulla (Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015) in light of this connection pattern shows that there are separate 'yellow' and 'pale' circuits that could be used for discriminating long and short-wavelength UV inputs.
evidence: This is inferred from the EM reconstruction analysis showing distinct connectivity patterns.

claim: Tm5a projection neurons are selectively connected to yR7 PRs.
source: The yellow circuit might be constructed using DIP-γ-Dpr11 interactions, since both yDm8 and Tm5a projection neurons, which are also selectively connected to yR7 PRs, express DIP-γ (Cosmanescu et al., 2018; Karuppudurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding and is also demonstrated in the EM reconstruction analysis (Figure 3).

claim: Tm5a projection neurons express DIP-γ.
source: The yellow circuit might be constructed using DIP-γ-Dpr11 interactions, since both yDm8 and Tm5a projection neurons, which are also selectively connected to yR7 PRs, express DIP-γ (Cosmanescu et al., 2018; Karuppudurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding.

claim: DIP-γ and Dpr11 are both required for normal morphogenesis of yDm8 distal dendrites.
source: DIP-γ and Dpr11 are both required for normal morphogenesis of yDm8 distal dendrites, which fasciculate with yR7 terminals and contain many of the R7-Dm8 synapses.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of mutant phenotypes in Figure 5.

claim: yDm8 distal dendrites fasciculate with yR7 terminals and contain many of the R7-Dm8 synapses.
source: DIP-γ and Dpr11 are both required for normal morphogenesis of yDm8 distal dendrites, which fasciculate with yR7 terminals and contain many of the R7-Dm8 synapses.
evidence: This is demonstrated through EM reconstruction and ExM analysis (Figures 4 and 6).

claim: DIP-γ-expressing yDm8 neurons are generated in excess during development.
source: Our results show that DIP-γ-expressing yDm8 neurons are generated in excess during development and compete for presynaptic yR7 partners.
evidence: This is demonstrated through developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A).

claim: yR7 PRs and yDm8 neurons recognize each other using Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
source: yR7 PRs and yDm8 neurons recognize each other using Dpr11- DIP-γ interactions.
evidence: This is demonstrated through gain-of-function experiments where Dpr11 expression in all R7 leads to selection of yDm8 (Figure 9).

claim: The engagement of DIP-γ by Dpr11 is necessary for generation of signals that allow yDm8 neurons to survive.
source: The engagement of DIP-γ by Dpr11 is necessary for generation of signals that allow yDm8 neurons to survive.
evidence: This is demonstrated through loss-of-function experiments showing yDm8 cell death in mutants (Figures 7 and 8).

claim: yR7 and pR7 ommatidia are present at a ~65y:35p ratio.
source: yR7 and pR7 ommatidia are present at a ~65y:35p ratio, and because of retinotopy we expect to find a similar ratio of y and p columns in the medulla.
evidence: This is a cited fact from the literature (Viets et al., 2016).

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 neurons in wild-type are present at a ratio of 60y:40p.
source: We find that yDm8 and pDm8 neurons in wild-type are present at a ratio of 60y:40p, which is comparable to the ratio of the input R7 PRs (Figure 1B,H–I) (Viets et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 1H-I).

claim: The arbor of each Dm8 contacts 12–16 medulla columns.
source: The arbor of each Dm8 contacts 12–16 medulla columns, but most synapses are made with the R7 in the central (home) column (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Gao et al., 2008; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature and confirmed in the current study.

claim: Most Dm8 synapses are made with the R7 in the central (home) column.
source: The arbor of each Dm8 contacts 12–16 medulla columns, but most synapses are made with the R7 in the central (home) column (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Gao et al., 2008; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature and confirmed through EM reconstruction analysis.

claim: The thick bundle of dendritic processes at the center of the Dm8 arbor makes extensive contacts with the R7 home column and contains the majority of R7-Dm8 synapses.
source: The thick bundle of dendritic processes at the center of the arbor makes extensive contacts with the R7 home column, and contains the majority of R7-Dm8 synapses (Figures 2A and 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through EM reconstruction analysis (Figures 2A and 3).

claim: The central dendritic projections of Dm8 extend distally from M6 to M4.
source: These central dendritic projections extend distally from M6 to M4, and we have denoted them as the 'sprig' of a Dm8 arbor.
evidence: This is observed in EM reconstruction and ExM images.

claim: The sprig of each Dm8 tiles the medulla.
source: The lateral arbor of each Dm8 overlaps extensively with other Dm8 arbors, but the center of highest arbor density, the sprig, tiles the medulla.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the coverage pattern indicates approximately one cell per column.

claim: All yDm8 flipouts using the split-GAL4 driver contacted yR7 home columns (43/43 clones).
source: Using the yDm8 split-GAL4 driver, we exclusively labeled Dm8 neurons that have yR7 as the home column (43/43 flipouts; Figure 2B,D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments.

claim: yDm8 specifically innervate yR7 and avoid pR7 in the home column.
source: This indicates that yDm8 specifically innervate yR7 and avoid pR7 in the home column.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that all yDm8 flipouts contacted yR7 home columns.

claim: yDm8 with two home columns occur at a frequency of ~6% (4/64 clones).
source: We also observed yDm8 with two home columns at a frequency of ~6% (4/64 clones) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments.

claim: All four two-home column yDm8 had both sprigs on yR7 columns.
source: All four had both sprigs on yR7 columns (see Figure 5H for an example).
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments.

claim: Single-cell clones of pDm8 innervate only pR7 (21 pDm8 clones analyzed; one had two pR7 home columns).
source: Single-cell clones of pDm8 were found to innervate only pR7 (21 pDm8 clones were analyzed; one had two pR7 home columns) (Figure 2C,E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through single-cell flipout experiments.

claim: DIP-γ labeling is seen in the M6 layer only under yR7 that co-express Dpr11 and Chp, and not under pR7 that are labeled with Chp alone.
source: DIP-γ labeling is seen in the M6 layer only under yR7 that co-express Dpr11 and Chp, and not under pR7 that are labeled with Chp alone (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunohistochemistry (Figure 2F).

claim: There is no significant difference in the total number of R7 terminals contacted by yDm8 and pDm8 subtypes.
source: Cross-sectional (top-down) views show that although there is no significant difference in the total number of R7 terminals contacted by the two Dm8 subtypes, there is a bias in the type of R7 they contact (Figure 2D–E,I–J).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of single-cell clones (Figure 2J).

claim: yDm8 contacts with yR7 columns were significantly higher (~15%) than pDm8 connections with yR7.
source: yDm8 contacts with yR7 columns were significantly higher (~15%) than pDm8 connections with yR7.
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of single-cell clones (Figure 2I).

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 populations have independent origins.
source: Figure 2G shows that there are gaps in the M6 layer, indicating that the two Dm8 subtypes are in fact separate populations.
evidence: This is demonstrated through conditional labeling experiments (Figure 2G).

claim: Most R7 output synapses are made onto Dm8, Dm9, Tm5a, Tm5b, and Tm5c.
source: Most R7 output synapses are made onto Dm8, Dm9 (a multicolumnar medulla intrinsic neuron), Tm5a, Tm5b, and Tm5c (Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Tm5a/b/c neurons project to the lobula and are likely to be the main output neurons of R7 circuits.
source: Tm5a/b/c neurons project to the lobula, and are likely to be the main output neurons of R7 circuits.
evidence: This is inferred from anatomical observations and cited literature.

claim: The main dendritic branch of Tm5a associates with yR7 but not with pR7 axons.
source: However, the main dendritic branch of Tm5a was found to associate with yR7 but not with pR7 axons in a light-level analysis (Karuppudurai et al., 2014), suggesting that yR7 selectively synapses onto Tm5a.
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Five yR7 PRs (in columns A, E, F, J, and K) and three pR7 PRs (in columns Home, B and D) were identified in the EM reconstruction.
source: Using this hypothesis as a guide, we identified five candidate yR7 PRs (in columns A, E, F, J, and K) and three pR7 PRs (in columns Home, B and D) (Figure 3; y/p column identity indicated in diagram).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the EM reconstruction using Tm5a connectivity as a guide.

claim: Each R7 makes many more output synapses onto its home column Dm8 than onto other Dm8 neurons.
source: Each R7 makes many more output synapses onto its home column Dm8 than onto other Dm8 neurons, allowing us to identify B/home and D as pDm8, while A, E, F, J, and K are yDm8 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: The five yR7 make output synapses only onto Tm5a and not Tm5b.
source: The five yR7 make output synapses only onto Tm5a and not Tm5b, which was the basis for their assignment as y (Karuppudurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: The three pR7 synapse onto Tm5b and not Tm5a.
source: The three pR7 synapse onto Tm5b and not Tm5a (Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: Tm5a and Tm5b represent separate output channels for y (Rh4) and p (Rh3) inputs.
source: Thus, Tm5a and Tm5b represent separate output channels for y (Rh4) and p (Rh3) inputs for this set of columns (see Figure 3—source data 1 legend).
evidence: This is inferred from the selective connectivity patterns observed in the EM reconstruction.

claim: Tm5a expresses DIP-γ, while Tm5b does not.
source: Tm5a expresses DIP-γ, while Tm5b does not (Cosmanescu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: The selective connection of yR7 to both yDm8 and Tm5a in the home column might involve Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
source: This suggests that the selective connection of yR7 to both yDm8 and Tm5a in the home column might involve Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both yDm8 and Tm5a express DIP-γ and connect to Dpr11-expressing yR7.

claim: Dm8 output synapses onto Tm5a/b have a similar specificity to the R7 output synapses.
source: We find that Dm8 output synapses onto Tm5a/b have a similar specificity to the R7 output synapses.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: Both pDm8 neurons almost exclusively synapse onto Tm5b and not Tm5a.
source: Both pDm8 neurons almost exclusively synapse onto Tm5b and not Tm5a, and four of the five yDm8 neurons (E, F, J and K) make more synapses onto Tm5a than Tm5b (yDm8-A, however, makes 10 synapses onto Tm5b-home and only five onto Tm5a-A; Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: Four of the five yDm8 neurons (E, F, J and K) make more synapses onto Tm5a than Tm5b.
source: Both pDm8 neurons almost exclusively synapse onto Tm5b and not Tm5a, and four of the five yDm8 neurons (E, F, J and K) make more synapses onto Tm5a than Tm5b (yDm8-A, however, makes 10 synapses onto Tm5b-home and only five onto Tm5a-A; Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: Each Dm9 receives input from both types of R7 and Dm8, and makes output synapses onto multiple R7 neurons.
source: Each Dm9 receives input from both types of R7 and Dm8, and makes output synapses onto multiple R7 neurons (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction.

claim: R7 synapses are polyadic, and Dm8 and Tm5a/b often sit together at synaptic sites.
source: R7 synapses are polyadic, and Dm8 and Tm5a/b often sit together at synaptic sites.
evidence: This is demonstrated through EM sections (Figure 4D and E).

claim: In column E, the yR7-E axon terminal, yDm8-E sprig, and Tm5a-E dendritic branch are tightly wrapped around each other.
source: In column E, the yR7-E axon terminal, yDm8-E sprig, and Tm5a-E dendritic branch are tightly wrapped around each other (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through 3D rendering of the EM reconstruction (Figure 4A,B).

claim: yR7-E T-bars are distributed in layers M4-M6, and are apposed to postsynapses in the yDm8-E sprig and the distal dendritic branch of the Tm5a-E neuron.
source: yR7-E T-bars are distributed in layers M4-M6, and are apposed to postsynapses in the yDm8-E sprig and the distal dendritic branch of the Tm5a-E neuron (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through 3D rendering of the EM reconstruction (Figure 4B).

claim: Most yDm8-E output synapses are onto Tm5a-E and Dm9, and these are distributed between the sprig in M4-M5 and the main arbor in M6.
source: Most yDm8-E output synapses are onto Tm5a-E and Dm9 (Figure 3 and Figure 3—source data 1), and these are distributed between the sprig in M4-M5 and the main arbor in M6 (Figure 4B and associated Figure 4—videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3, Figure 4B).

claim: pDm8-D has a very thin sprig, and most pR7-D and pDm8-D T-bars are in M6.
source: Although pDm8 usually have robust sprigs (e.g. Figure 2C), pDm8-D has a very thin sprig, and most pR7-D and pDm8-D T-bars are in M6 (Figure 4A,C and associated Figure 4—videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated through 3D rendering of the EM reconstruction (Figure 4A,C).

claim: Maximum sprig diameter was significantly decreased in both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants compared to control.
source: Maximum sprig diameter was significantly decreased in both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants compared to control, but the height of the sprig was relatively unaffected (Figure 5C–F,I,K).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5I).

claim: The height of the sprig was relatively unaffected in dpr11 mutants.
source: Maximum sprig diameter was significantly decreased in both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants compared to control, but the height of the sprig was relatively unaffected (Figure 5C–F,I,K).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5K).

claim: The numbers of two-home column single cell clones were higher in DIP-γ mutants as compared to controls.
source: The numbers of two-home column single cell clones (with two sprigs) were higher in DIP-γ mutants as compared to controls (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5G).

claim: There was no difference in the percentage of yR7 columns contacted by yDm8 in either DIP-γ or dpr11 mutants.
source: There was no difference in the percentage of yR7 columns contacted in either mutant, but yDm8 neurons in the DIP-γ mutant displayed an increase over control in the total number of columns contacted.
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5L).

claim: yDm8 neurons in the DIP-γ mutant displayed an increase over control in the total number of columns contacted.
source: There was no difference in the percentage of yR7 columns contacted in either mutant, but yDm8 neurons in the DIP-γ mutant displayed an increase over control in the total number of columns contacted.
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5J).

claim: The yDm8-E sprig and Tm5a-E dendritic branch are both wrapped tightly around the yR7-E terminal, and most yR7 T-bars are apposed to the sprig and branch within layer M5.
source: The yDm8-E sprig and Tm5a-E dendritic branch are both wrapped tightly around the yR7-E terminal, and most yR7 T-bars are apposed to the sprig and branch within layer M5.
evidence: This is demonstrated through 3D rendering of the EM reconstruction (Figure 4B).

claim: 3D renderings of wild-type yDm8 and yR7 neurons from ExM are almost superimposable on yDm8-E and yR7-E from the EM reconstruction.
source: Remarkably, our 3D renderings of wild-type yDm8 and yR7 neurons from ExM (Figure 6 and associated videos) are almost superimposable on yDm8-E and yR7-E from the EM reconstruction (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through comparison of ExM and EM images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).

claim: R7 is histaminergic and inhibits both Dm8 and Tm5a/b.
source: R7 is histaminergic, and inhibits both Dm8 and Tm5a/b (Figure 11A–B), usually through polyadic synapses where a single R7 T-bar is apposed to both a Dm8 and a Tm5a/b postysnapse (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: This is based on cited literature and EM reconstruction analysis.

claim: Dm8 is glutamatergic.
source: Dm8 is glutamatergic, while Tm5a and Tm5b are cholinergic (Davis et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Tm5a and Tm5b are cholinergic.
source: Dm8 is glutamatergic, while Tm5a and Tm5b are cholinergic (Davis et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: yR7 input might cause inhibition of Tm5a in two ways: by direct inhibition and by inhibiting the glutamatergic input of yDm8 onto Tm5a.
source: This suggests that yR7 input might cause inhibition of Tm5a in two ways: by direct inhibition and by inhibiting the glutamatergic input (probably excitatory) of yDm8 onto Tm5a.
evidence: This is inferred from the connectivity patterns and neurotransmitter identities.

claim: pR7 input could preferentially inhibit Tm5b by both direct and indirect mechanisms.
source: Conversely, pR7 input could preferentially inhibit Tm5b by both direct and indirect mechanisms.
evidence: This is inferred from the connectivity patterns and neurotransmitter identities.

claim: Both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants showed a ~50% decrease in yDm8 cell number using the pan-Dm8 driver.
source: Both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants showed a ~ 50% decrease in yDm8 cell number using the pan-Dm8 driver and 60–65% loss when determined with Dac (Figure 7A,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7A,C).

claim: Both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants showed 60–65% loss of yDm8 when determined with Dac.
source: Both DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants showed a ~ 50% decrease in yDm8 cell number using the pan-Dm8 driver and 60–65% loss when determined with Dac (Figure 7A,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7A,C).

claim: A double mutant of DIP-γ and dpr11 had a similar phenotype to the two single mutants.
source: A double mutant had a similar phenotype to the two single mutants (Figure 7A), suggesting that the two genes function in the same pathway(s).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7A).

claim: The two genes DIP-γ and dpr11 function in the same pathway(s).
source: A double mutant had a similar phenotype to the two single mutants (Figure 7A), suggesting that the two genes function in the same pathway(s).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the double mutant phenotype is not more severe than single mutants.

claim: The loss of yDm8 in DIP-γ mutants was partially rescued by expressing a DIP-γ transgene using the DIP-γ Gal4 driver.
source: The loss of yDm8 in DIP-γ mutants was partially rescued by expressing a DIP-γ transgene using the DIP-γ Gal4 driver (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7A).

claim: Eye-specific dpr11 transgenic RNAi resulted in a ~40% reduction in yDm8 cell numbers.
source: To determine if yDm8 loss in dpr11 mutants was due to the absence of Dpr11 from the eye or from other Dpr11-expressing cells in the medulla, we performed eye-specific dpr11 transgenic RNAi, and found a ~ 40% reduction in yDm8 cell numbers (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7C).

claim: yDm8 neurons are born in excess of the final cell numbers that are present in the adult.
source: There are two subtypes of Dm8: yDm8 that express DIP-γ and pDm8 that do not. yDm8 are born in excess of the final cell numbers that are present in the adult (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A).

claim: Dpr11 is expressed exclusively in yR7 in the retina.
source: Dpr11, the binding partner of DIP-γ, is expressed exclusively in yR7 in the retina (Figure 1E–F), allowing yDm8 neurons to select yR7 PRs as their appropriate partners.
evidence: This is demonstrated through reporter expression analysis (Figure 1E-F).

claim: The extra yDm8 that do not find a yR7 partner undergo cell death due to loss of survival signals mediated by DIP-γ-Dpr11 interactions.
source: The extra yDm8 that do not find a yR7 partner undergo cell death due to loss of survival signals mediated by DIP-γ-Dpr11 interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that yDm8 die in DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants and can be rescued by DIAP.

claim: This selection mechanism ensures that the ratio of yDm8 to pDm8 in the medulla matches the ratio of yR7 to pR7 in the eye.
source: This selection mechanism ensures that the ratio of yDm8 to pDm8 in the medulla matches the ratio of yR7 to pR7 in the eye (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments showing matching ratios (Figure 1I).

claim: 50–60% of yDm8 die when either DIP-γ or Dpr11 is absent.
source: Dpr11 and DIP-γ are required for survival, because 50–60% of yDm8 die when either molecule is absent (Figures 7, 8A and 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments in mutants (Figures 7, 8A).

claim: If all R7 are converted to yR7 (in ssGOF), or if they all express Dpr11, many more yDm8 neurons survive than in wild-type.
source: If all R7 are converted to yR7 (in ssGOF), or if they all express Dpr11, many more yDm8 neurons survive than in wild-type, showing that the numbers of Dpr11-expressing R7 are limiting for yDm8 survival in wild-type animals (Figures 9C and 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments in gain-of-function genotypes (Figure 9C).

claim: The numbers of Dpr11-expressing R7 are limiting for yDm8 survival in wild-type animals.
source: If all R7 are converted to yR7 (in ssGOF), or if they all express Dpr11, many more yDm8 neurons survive than in wild-type, showing that the numbers of Dpr11-expressing R7 are limiting for yDm8 survival in wild-type animals (Figures 9C and 10).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that more yDm8 survive when more R7 express Dpr11.

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 populations do not compete with each other in wild-type because they have different R7 subtype partners.
source: yDm8 and pDm8 populations do not compete with each other in wild-type because they have different R7 subtype partners.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that pDm8 numbers do not change when yDm8 are rescued with DIAP.

claim: When the numbers of yDm8 neurons are increased by suppressing apoptotic cell death with DIAP in yDm8, pDm8 cell numbers do not decrease.
source: When the numbers of yDm8 neurons are increased by suppressing apoptotic cell death with DIAP in yDm8, pDm8 cell numbers do not decrease (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 7B).

claim: yDm8 and pDm8 neurons can be forced to compete by changing R7 subtype fate.
source: However, yDm8 and pDm8 neurons can be forced to compete by changing R7 subtype fate.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments where R7 fates are altered (Figure 9).

claim: When all R7 PRs are converted to yR7, or when they all express Dpr11, almost all pDm8 neurons die.
source: When all R7 PRs are converted to yR7, or when they all express Dpr11, almost all pDm8 neurons die (Figures 9D and 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 9D).

claim: Most yDm8 neurons die when all R7 PRs are converted to pR7.
source: Conversely, most yDm8 neurons die when all R7 PRs are converted to pR7 (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 9G).

claim: pDm8 neurons are preferentially selected by pR7 PRs, using unknown molecular mechanisms.
source: pDm8 neurons are preferentially selected by pR7 PRs, using unknown molecular mechanisms, and pR7 PRs are needed to ensure pDm8 survival.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that pDm8 die when R7 are absent or converted to yR7.

claim: pR7 PRs are needed to ensure pDm8 survival.
source: pDm8 neurons are preferentially selected by pR7 PRs, using unknown molecular mechanisms, and pR7 PRs are needed to ensure pDm8 survival.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments showing pDm8 loss when R7 are absent or converted to yR7.

claim: pDm8 are unable to effectively fill vacant yR7 slots.
source: This is demonstrated by the fact that pDm8 are unable to effectively fill vacant yR7 slots.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the observation that in ssGOF, DIP-γ mutants, pDm8 numbers only increase by ~30 despite ~180 vacant yR7 slots.

claim: In ssGOF, DIP-γ animals, there are at least 180 yR7 slots that are made vacant by loss of yDm8, but the number of pDm8 neurons only increases by ~30 (~2 fold) in this genotype.
source: For example, in ssGOF, DIP-γ animals, there are at least 180 yR7 slots that are made vacant by loss of yDm8, but the number of pDm8 neurons only increases by ~30 (~2 fold) in this genotype (Figure 9C–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figure 9C-D).

claim: Dpr11 is already expressed in a subset of R7 PRs at 15 hr APF, indicating that yR7 fate is determined by that time.
source: Dpr11 is already expressed in a subset of R7 PRs at 15 hr APF, indicating that yR7 fate is determined by that time (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through reporter expression analysis at 15 hr APF (Figure 8F).

claim: DIP-γ is expressed by 18 hr - 20 hr APF in select Dm8 neurons apposed to Dpr11-expressing R7 PRs.
source: DIP-γ is expressed by 18 hr - 20 hr APF in select Dm8 neurons apposed to Dpr11-expressing R7 PRs (Figure 8G; Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunohistochemistry at 18-20 hr APF (Figure 8G).

claim: At 18-20 hr APF, R7 growth cones are positioned in the incipient layer.
source: At this time, R7 growth cones are positioned in the incipient layer (Kulkarni et al., 2016; Ting et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Single-cell Dm8 clones contact home column R7 growth cones by 17 hr APF.
source: This is consistent with earlier findings that single-cell Dm8 clones contact home column R7 growth cones by 17 hr APF (Ting et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: yR7 and yDm8 have met and selected each other in the incipient layer by 15 hr - 20 hr APF.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that yR7 and yDm8 have met and selected each other in the incipient layer by 15 hr - 20 hr APF.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of Dpr11 and DIP-γ expression and R7 growth cone positioning.

claim: Survival signaling mediated by Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions is probably initiated around 15-20 hr APF.
source: Survival signaling mediated by Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions is probably initiated around that time, because cell death of yDm8 in DIP-γ mutants begins to occur between 15 hr and 25 hr APF (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of yDm8 cell death in mutants.

claim: Cell death of yDm8 in DIP-γ mutants begins to occur between 15 hr and 25 hr APF.
source: Survival signaling mediated by Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions is probably initiated around that time, because cell death of yDm8 in DIP-γ mutants begins to occur between 15 hr and 25 hr APF (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A).

claim: There is widespread cell death in the medullary cortex as part of normal optic lobe development.
source: There is widespread cell death in the medullary cortex as part of normal optic lobe development.
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature (Togane et al., 2012).

claim: Cell death in the medullary cortex occurs in two phases, with the first phase spanning 0 hr - 48 hr APF and peaking at 24 hr APF.
source: This occurs in two phases, with the first phase spanning 0 hr - 48 hr APF and peaking at 24 hr APF (Togane et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: In wild-type, ~30% of the yDm8 neurons present at 15 hr APF die by 45 hr APF.
source: In wild-type, ~30% of the yDm8 neurons present at 15 hr APF die by 45 hr APF, at which time yDm8 cell numbers are the same as those in adult.
evidence: This is demonstrated through developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A).

claim: In DIP-γ mutants, ~75% of yDm8 are lost by 45 hr APF.
source: In DIP-γ mutants, ~75% are lost by 45 hr APF.
evidence: This is demonstrated through developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A).

claim: If apoptotic cell death is suppressed by DIAP, then the yDm8 population in adult remains the same as at 15 hr APF.
source: If apoptotic cell death is suppressed by DIAP, then the yDm8 population in adult remains the same as at 15 hr APF (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments with DIAP rescue (Figure 8A).

claim: The yDm8 neurons that die in wild-type are those that are in excess of the number that can be selected for survival by Dpr11-expressing yR7 PRs.
source: We suggest that the yDm8 neurons that die in wild-type are those that are in excess of the number that can be selected for survival by Dpr11-expressing yR7 PRs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that more yDm8 survive when more R7 express Dpr11.

claim: The excess yDm8 neurons in wild-type die because they lack survival signals that are transmitted through Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
source: Since most yDm8 neurons require DIP-γ for survival, we infer that the excess yDm8 neurons in wild-type die because they lack survival signals that are transmitted through Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that yDm8 die in DIP-γ mutants.

claim: These selection events are independent of synaptogenesis between R7 and Dm8, which occurs only after 60 hr APF.
source: These selection events are independent of synaptogenesis between R7 and Dm8, which occurs only after 60 hr APF.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of cell death (before 45 hr APF) versus synaptogenesis (after 60 hr APF).

claim: DIP-α-expressing Dm4 neurons are generated in excess, and their survival is regulated by interactions between DIP-α and its partners Dprs 6 and 10.
source: The DIP-α-expressing Dm4 neurons are also generated in excess, and their survival is regulated by interactions between DIP-α and its partners Dprs 6 and 10, which are expressed on presynaptic L3 neurons.
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study (Xu et al., 2018).

claim: In DIP-α or dpr6 dpr10 mutants, about 50% of Dm4 and 20% of Dm12 neurons are lost.
source: In DIP-α or dpr6 dpr10 mutants, about 50% of Dm4 and 20% of Dm12 neurons are lost.
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study (Xu et al., 2018).

claim: If cell death is blocked in wild-type, the cell numbers of Dm4 neurons in adults are increased by about 25%.
source: If cell death is blocked in wild-type, the cell numbers of Dm4 neurons in adults are increased by about 25% (Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study.

claim: Not all DIP-γ expressing neurons in the optic lobe require it for survival.
source: However, not all DIP-γ expressing neurons in the optic lobe require it for survival.
evidence: This is stated based on unpublished observations.

claim: A subset of lobula plate tangential cells (LPTCs) express DIP-γ, and these do not die in DIP-γ mutants.
source: A subset of lobula plate tangential cells (LPTCs) also express DIP-γ, and these do not die in DIP-γ mutants (unpublished data).
evidence: This is stated based on unpublished observations.

claim: When Dpr11 is expressed in all R7, all pDm8 home columns are converted to yDm8.
source: Our gain-of-function studies show that when Dpr11 is expressed in all R7, all pDm8 home columns are converted to yDm8 (Figure 9E–F,H), demonstrating that expression of Dpr11 in R7 PRs that are otherwise of the pale subtype is sufficient for selection of yDm8.
evidence: This is demonstrated through gain-of-function experiments (Figure 9E-F,H).

claim: Expression of Dpr11 in R7 PRs that are otherwise of the pale subtype is sufficient for selection of yDm8.
source: Our gain-of-function studies show that when Dpr11 is expressed in all R7, all pDm8 home columns are converted to yDm8 (Figure 9E–F,H), demonstrating that expression of Dpr11 in R7 PRs that are otherwise of the pale subtype is sufficient for selection of yDm8.
evidence: This is demonstrated through gain-of-function experiments (Figure 9E-F,H).

claim: We did not observe mistargeting of surviving yDm8 in dpr11 mutants to pR7 columns, most likely because pR7 slots are occupied by pDm8 neurons.
source: We did not observe mistargeting of surviving yDm8 in dpr11 mutants to pR7 columns, most likely because pR7 slots are occupied by pDm8 neurons (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of mutants at 44 hr APF (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A-D).

claim: There may be a second mechanism for support (and possibly selection) of yDm8 by R7 that is independent of Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
source: Another factor that could contribute to accurate targeting in dpr11 mutants is that there may be a second mechanism for support (and possibly selection) of yDm8 by R7 that is independent of Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that ~70% of yDm8 are lost in sev mutants but only ~50% in DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants.

claim: ~70% of yDm8 are lost in sev mutants, but only ~50% in DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants.
source: This is suggested by the fact that ~70% of yDm8 are lost in sev mutants, but only ~50% in DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants (Figures 9C and 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell counting experiments (Figures 9C and 7A).

claim: In DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants, the distribution of sprig diameters for yDm8 neurons is shifted toward smaller values.
source: In DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants, the distribution of sprig diameters for yDm8 neurons is shifted toward smaller values (Figure 5I), suggesting that mutant sprigs may have a reduced capacity to form synapses with yR7 in M4 and M5.
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5I).

claim: Mutant sprigs may have a reduced capacity to form synapses with yR7 in M4 and M5.
source: In DIP-γ and dpr11 mutants, the distribution of sprig diameters for yDm8 neurons is shifted toward smaller values (Figure 5I), suggesting that mutant sprigs may have a reduced capacity to form synapses with yR7 in M4 and M5.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of reduced sprig diameter in mutants.

claim: Synapses that would have been in M4 and M5 might be found in the base of the arbor in M6 in mutants.
source: Synapses that would have been in M4 and M5 might then be found in the base of the arbor in M6.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation of reduced sprig diameter and comparison with EM reconstruction data.

claim: R7 output synapses (T-bars) are mainly in M4 and M5 (on the sprig) in column E, which has a Dm8 with a thick sprig.
source: EM reconstruction data for columns D and E supports this idea. R7 output synapses (T-bars) are mainly in M4 and M5 (on the sprig) in column E, which has a Dm8 with a thick sprig (Figures 2A and 4A, inset in 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figures 2A and 4A, inset in 4B).

claim: In column D, whose Dm8 has a very thin sprig, R7 T-bars are located in M6 (in the main arbor).
source: In column D, whose Dm8 has a very thin sprig, R7 T-bars are located in M6 (in the main arbor) (Figure 4A, inset in 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 4A, inset in 4C).

claim: The effects of Dpr11 and DIP-γ on yDm8 sprig morphology may involve a different pathway from that involved in cell death.
source: The effects of Dpr11 and DIP-γ on yDm8 sprig morphology may involve a different pathway from that involved in cell death.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that sprig defects are present in surviving neurons in adults.

claim: Sprig morphology defects might be a consequence of a loss of Dpr11-DIP-γ-mediated adhesion between yR7 and yDm8.
source: Sprig morphology defects might be a consequence of a loss of Dpr11-DIP-γ-mediated adhesion between yR7 and yDm8, since dpr11 and DIP-γ mutants are similarly affected.
evidence: This is speculated based on the similar phenotypes in both mutants.

claim: An 'overshoot' phenotype was reported in dpr11Mi>GFP/Df mutants in which some R7 terminals had processes extending beyond M6 into proximal medulla layers.
source: We had earlier reported an 'overshoot' phenotype in dpr11Mi>GFP/Df mutants in which some R7 terminals had processes extending beyond M6 into proximal medulla layers (Carrillo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study.

claim: This overshoot phenotype was not observed in the dpr11CRISPR null mutant when endogenous Brp puncta were labeled with the STaR method.
source: However, this phenotype was not observed in the dpr11CRISPR null mutant when endogenous Brp puncta were labeled with the STaR method (Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited finding from a previous study.

claim: A significant increase in yR7 overshoots was observed in dpr11CRISPR homozygotes using Brp-short as compared with the heterozygous control.
source: To determine whether this discrepancy was due to the dpr11Mi>GFP/Df genotype or to the Brp-short marker, we analyzed dpr11CRISPR homozygotes using Brp-short and observed a significant increase in yR7 overshoots as compared with the heterozygous control (Figure 9—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis using Brp-short marker (Figure 9—figure supplement 2E).

claim: The interpretation of the Brp-short phenotype is unclear, as it does not correspond to a shift in the distribution of endogenous Brp puncta into layers proximal to M6.
source: However, the interpretation of this Brp-short phenotype is unclear, as it does not correspond to a shift in the distribution of endogenous Brp puncta into layers proximal to M6.
evidence: This is stated based on comparison of Brp-short and endogenous Brp labeling results.

claim: Tm5a, Tm5b, and Tm5c are output neurons for R7 and R8 circuits.
source: Tm5a, Tm5b, and Tm5c are output neurons for R7 and R8 circuits.
evidence: This is based on cited literature and anatomical observations.

claim: Tm5a/b/c dendrites receive direct synaptic input from R7, R8, and Dm8.
source: Their dendrites receive direct synaptic input from R7, R8, and Dm8, and their axons relay signals to the lobula (Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Tm5a/b/c axons relay signals to the lobula.
source: Their dendrites receive direct synaptic input from R7, R8, and Dm8, and their axons relay signals to the lobula (Gao et al., 2008; Karuppudurai et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Tm5a/b/c cells are analogous to vertebrate retinal ganglion cells.
source: It has been hypothesized that Tm5a/b/c cells are analogous to vertebrate retinal ganglion cells, and that true color vision (intensity-independent hue discrimination) involves interpretation of Tm inputs by circuits in the lobula.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the text.

claim: True color vision (intensity-independent hue discrimination) involves interpretation of Tm inputs by circuits in the lobula.
source: It has been hypothesized that Tm5a/b/c cells are analogous to vertebrate retinal ganglion cells, and that true color vision (intensity-independent hue discrimination) involves interpretation of Tm inputs by circuits in the lobula.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the text.

claim: Chi-Hon Lee and colleagues developed a learning paradigm in which flies discriminate between equiluminant blue and green light.
source: Chi-Hon Lee and his colleagues developed a learning paradigm in which flies discriminate between equiluminant blue and green light, which are differentially sensed by y (Rh6) and p (Rh5) R8.
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature (Melnattur et al., 2014).

claim: Four classes of Tm neurons (Tm5 a/b/c and Tm20) make redundant contributions to the blue-green discrimination response.
source: Four classes of Tm neurons (Tm5 a/b/c and Tm20) make redundant contributions to this response (Melnattur et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: The absorption spectra of Rh4 (yR7) and Rh3 (pR7) extensively overlap.
source: The absorption spectra of Rh4 (yR7) and Rh3 (pR7) extensively overlap (Figure 11C), and it is unlikely that a learned color vision paradigm could be developed that would distinguish between Rh4 and Rh3 inputs.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 11C and is based on known rhodopsin properties.

claim: It is unlikely that a learned color vision paradigm could be developed that would distinguish between Rh4 and Rh3 inputs.
source: The absorption spectra of Rh4 (yR7) and Rh3 (pR7) extensively overlap (Figure 11C), and it is unlikely that a learned color vision paradigm could be developed that would distinguish between Rh4 and Rh3 inputs.
evidence: This is inferred from the extensive overlap of absorption spectra.

claim: The existence of discrete y and p R7 channels suggests that the fly utilizes them to make discriminations among UV wavelength inputs.
source: Nevertheless, the existence of discrete y and p R7 channels suggests that the fly utilizes them to make discriminations among UV wavelength inputs.
evidence: This is inferred from the existence of separate circuits.

claim: To make discriminations among UV wavelengths would require that the y and p channels have different synaptic circuits with distinguishable outputs.
source: To make such discriminations would require that the y and p channels have different synaptic circuits with distinguishable outputs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the requirements for wavelength discrimination.

claim: yR7 and yDm8 both preferentially synapse onto Tm5a, while pR7 and pDm8 synapse onto Tm5b.
source: Our analysis of the patterns of synaptic connections defined by the EM reconstruction of the medulla (Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015) indicates that yR7 and yDm8 both preferentially synapse onto Tm5a, while pR7 and pDm8 synapse onto Tm5b (Figure 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3).

claim: Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions might be involved in specifying both yR7-yDm8 and yR7-Tm5a connections.
source: Tm5a expresses DIP-γ, while Tm5b does not (Cosmanescu et al., 2018), so Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions might be involved in specifying both yR7-yDm8 and yR7-Tm5a connections.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression patterns and connectivity.

claim: Four of the seven Dm8 neurons, and three of the eight R7 PRs, make a few synapses onto Tm5c neurons.
source: Four of the seven Dm8 neurons, and three of the eight R7 PRs, also make a few synapses onto Tm5c neurons, which are required for innate UV preference (Karuppudurai et al., 2014) (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3—source data 1).

claim: Tm5c neurons are required for innate UV preference.
source: Four of the seven Dm8 neurons, and three of the eight R7 PRs, also make a few synapses onto Tm5c neurons, which are required for innate UV preference (Karuppudurai et al., 2014) (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: There is no specificity for y vs. p in the connections to Tm5c.
source: There is no specificity for y vs. p in the connections to Tm5c.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3—source data 1).

claim: Longer-wave inputs that activate Rh4 on yR7 more than Rh3 on pR7 might cause more inhibition of Tm5a than of Tm5b.
source: However, longer-wave inputs that activate Rh4 on yR7 more than Rh3 on pR7 might cause more inhibition of Tm5a than of Tm5b, while the reverse would be true of shorter-wave inputs that preferentially activate Rh3 on pR7 (Figure 11).
evidence: This is inferred from the absorption spectra and connectivity patterns.

claim: Shorter-wave inputs that preferentially activate Rh3 on pR7 might cause more inhibition of Tm5b than of Tm5a.
source: However, longer-wave inputs that activate Rh4 on yR7 more than Rh3 on pR7 might cause more inhibition of Tm5a than of Tm5b, while the reverse would be true of shorter-wave inputs that preferentially activate Rh3 on pR7 (Figure 11).
evidence: This is inferred from the absorption spectra and connectivity patterns.

claim: Combining direct (R7→Tm5a/b) and indirect (R7→Dm8→Tm5a/b) inhibition of Tm5a and Tm5b outputs might amplify wavelength discrimination effects.
source: Combining direct (R7→Tm5a/b) and indirect (R7→Dm8→Tm5a/b) inhibition of Tm5a and Tm5b outputs might amplify these effects, depending on the relative timing of R7 and Dm8 inputs.
evidence: This is speculated based on the circuit architecture.

claim: Neurons in the lobula or elsewhere that can read the ratio of Tm5a to Tm5b output might mediate UV wavelength discrimination.
source: This model suggests that neurons in the lobula or elsewhere that can read the ratio of Tm5a to Tm5b output mediate UV wavelength discrimination.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the circuit model.

claim: Tm5a/b/c and Tm20 as a group synapse onto many lobula neuron types.
source: Tm5a/b/c and Tm20 as a group synapse onto many lobula neuron types, but the specific partners of Tm5a and Tm5b are mostly unknown.
evidence: This is stated based on current knowledge.

claim: All Tm5a but only half of Tm5b neurons synapse onto LT11 lobula projection neurons.
source: Interestingly, however, all Tm5a but only half of Tm5b neurons synapse onto LT11 lobula projection neurons (Lin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Flies with silenced LT11 neurons have reduced phototaxis toward blue light.
source: Flies with silenced LT11 neurons have reduced phototaxis toward blue light (Otsuna et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a cited finding from the literature.

claim: Dpr11 and DIP-γ expression patterns define a yR7-yDm8-Tm5a color vision circuit that should preferentially respond to longer-wavelength UV input.
source: In conclusion, our results show that Dpr11 and DIP-γ expression patterns define a yR7-yDm8-Tm5a color vision circuit that should preferentially respond to longer-wavelength UV input.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results presented in the paper.

claim: Suppression of yDm8 cell death triggered by engagement of Dpr11 on yR7 by DIP-γ on yDm8 helps to build the yellow circuit by ensuring that each yDm8 has a home column yR7.
source: Suppression of yDm8 cell death triggered by engagement of Dpr11 on yR7 by DIP-γ on yDm8 helps to build this circuit by ensuring that each yDm8 has a home column yR7.
